title: A reverse reaction can create attracting oscillations
shortTitle: One reverse arrow changes the dynamics
oneLine: An explicit three-species mass-action network gains an attracting periodic orbit when one reverse reaction is restored, while the deleted network converges globally.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate gives explicit three-species mass-action counterexamples to three general isolated-intermediate reduction conjectures of Feliu and Kaihnsa. An integer-rate trimolecular network has a nondegenerate supercritical Hopf bifurcation, whereas deleting one reverse reaction leaves a system that converges globally to its unique positive equilibrium for every positive choice of the remaining rates. An exact one-parameter family classifies the first Lyapunov coefficient except at one explicitly isolated degenerate value. The result does not challenge the source paper's restricted theorem and does not resolve its motivating dual-phosphorylation question.

narration:
One reverse arrow changes the dynamics. An Evidence Press briefing.

Chemical reaction networks can behave very differently when a single reaction is made reversible. This candidate gives an exact example with three species. In the full network, restoring one reverse reaction produces a Hopf bifurcation and, on the certified side of the boundary, a small attracting periodic orbit. Remove that reverse reaction and the remaining system has one positive equilibrium and converges to it globally for every positive choice of the retained rates.

That contrast matters because a recent paper proposed three broad conjectures saying, in different forms, that deleting an isolated intermediate reaction should preserve the relevant spectral behaviour. The explicit network disproves those general conjectures. It does not challenge the paper's restricted theorem, and it does not settle the dual-phosphorylation problem that motivated the work.

The manuscript also studies a one-parameter family. Exact symbolic calculations locate the Hopf boundary and classify the first Lyapunov coefficient except at one isolated positive value where the cubic coefficient vanishes. The paper does not claim a Bautin bifurcation there, an amplitude certificate, or reaction-count minimality.

The evidence package contains the manuscript, reaction lists, exact certificates and replay code. Normal and optimized-wrapper runs reproduce the stated finite algebra, with the checker subprocess kept in ordinary assertion mode. The global convergence proof remains a written mathematical argument, not a proof-assistant formalisation.

This is an anonymous, AI-assisted and unrefereed research candidate. Internal checking is not external peer review or independent reproduction, and a bounded literature search is not proof of priority. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and adds no scientific evidence.
